x: For James Hilston it was over before it started, his hamstring problem rearing up again before the meet got under way and thus ruling him out of the foursome. Saturday saw the qualifying rounds of the Triple Jump get started and drawn in pool A, Phillips Idowu needed 15.50 to make the cut.

Phillips Idowu led through rounds one and two in the triple jump thanks to his opening 15.25. He improved again in round three with 15.33 but Birchfield's Wallace came through into the number one spot with his 15.35.
The welcome return by Phillips Idowu boosted morale of the horizontal jumpers, the average age of which was 17 years. All four in the long and triple came from our Youth and Junior squads!
Several leading juniors such as Phillips Idowu (TJ) were detained elsewhere for the best of reasons. But it is the sprints where the best potential remains for improvement.

Derek was holder of our longest survivng Club Record — a triple jump mark of 16.22m set as long ago as 1968 — until June 1998 when, 30 years and six days later, 19 year-old Phillips Idowu recorded 16.35m.
Pride of place must go to Phillips Idowu though - his 16.41 triple jump extended his Club Record by a further 6 cms. - and Mike Jones, who also set a new Belgrave best in the hammer.

… the men's athletics team: Sean Baldock, Darren Campbell, Ben Challenger, Dwain Chambers, Justin Chaston, Matt Douglas, Phillips Idowu and Chris Rawlinson; and Brendan Reilly has been picked for Ireland.…
A young man going places was Tim Abeyie who set two new personal records in the sprints but it was fellow Belgravian Phillips Idowu who won the man of the match award for his long jumping.
The flamboyant Phillips Idowu, sporting claret coloured hair, took just one attempt in the Triple Jump qualifying round - sailing out to 17.12 metres for a personal and Club record.

Among the next results, the discus found Kevin Brown in 2nd which was better than expected and Phillips Idowu was only 16 centimetres short of his best in winning the triple jump while the Frenchman fell short of his by some way; we were on song.

The long jump proved disappointing, the triple jump partly disappointing, as Phillips Idowu put in one 15m plus effort and went home, while the high jump was very satisfactory as Samson Oni, seeking a further qualifying mark of 2.15m for the World Juniors, could only manage 2.10m for second spot on count back.

And then our young tigers put the result beyond doubt as first Phillips Idowu doubled the triple and long jumps. A happy Samson Oni finished 4th in the high jump with a World Junior qualifying mark of 2.15m and was only denied victory on countback.

A dozen medallists at the AAA Championships included two winners - Mick Jones in the hammer and Phillips Idowu in triple jump. Vernicha James became our first global champion since John Regis when she won the World Junior 200 metre Championship in Jamaica.
Triple Jump - Phillips Idowu. In his first competition of the year Phillips was highly delighted to leap to 17.18m, only six inches behind his all time best.

Ben Challenger is Britain’s sole high jumper and Goldie Sayers is our women’s javelin representative. Phillips Idowu was originally named to take part in the triple jump - subject to fitness - but has now withdrawn.
